evaluations.claim: performance gap between the two methods is substantially wider on the Easy set
evaluations.reality: The gap is actually much wider on the Hard set (~0.2 vs ~0.0) than on the Easy set (~0.05 difference). This is a direct inversion of the key finding
evaluations.reason: Hard set gap is wider (~0.2 vs ~0.05).

evaluations.claim: LUFFY maintains a consistent lead of approximately 0.10 throughout training on Easy set
evaluations.reality: The gap on the Easy set is much smaller, approximately 0.03-0.05, not 0.10 — and the two lines are very close together for much of the training
evaluations.reason: Easy set gap is ~0.05, not consistently ~0.10.

evaluations.claim: trajectories only clearly diverge after step 200 on the Hard set
evaluations.reality: On the Hard set, the trajectories diverge much earlier — On-Policy drops to ~0.0 by step 100-150 while LUFFY continues climbing, so divergence is apparent by step 100
evaluations.reason: Divergence on Hard set starts by step 100-150.
